newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.12 up at 41.98 to the dollar in the kerb market on Tuesday on low demand for the U.S. currency at the yearend, dealers said.
The rupee is likely to open stable on Wednesday owing to bank holiday, one dealer said.
The State (central) bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 rupees to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 5.00 percent, compared to the opening at 4.80 percent.
